plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying that amount, and never overpay. Bidding above value risks winning at a price exceeding my value; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With value $24, the optimal bid is simply $24, regardless of opponents' bidding behavior.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $9, I should bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than value risks overpaying if you win; bidding lower risks losing profitable deals. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $13, so I will bid exactly that amount.
